description: Draft Batch 2 Windows ATT&CK mapping evaluation examples; labels require analyst review.

examples.text: A process runs whoami and hostname to discover the current security context and computer name.
A process runs ipconfig and route commands to discover network interface settings and routing information.
A process queries installed security products and antivirus status to identify defenses on the host.
A process enumerates running processes to identify applications and services currently executing.
A process lists files and directories in a user's document folder to discover available files.
A remote administration utility creates a Windows service on another host and uses it to execute a program.
A process uses PowerShell to download a script from an external server and execute the downloaded content.
A process exports browser-stored authentication cookies and sends them to an external destination.
A process modifies Windows Defender settings to disable real-time protection without authorization.
A process deletes local Windows event logs to remove records of its earlier activity.
An approved help-desk script runs whoami and hostname to record the computer and account in an asset inventory.
An IT administrator uses ipconfig to troubleshoot a user's network connectivity.
The approved endpoint security console checks antivirus installation and protection status across managed computers.
A system monitoring agent periodically enumerates running processes to report resource consumption.
A backup indexer lists files and directories to determine which documents require backup.
An authorized software deployment platform installs and starts a Windows service on a managed workstation.
An administrator downloads a signed software update from the vendor's official server and verifies its signature before installation.
A user signs in to an approved browser application, which stores session cookies for normal use.
An authorized security administrator temporarily changes antivirus settings during a documented maintenance procedure and restores protection afterward.
A Windows event-log retention policy removes old records according to the organization's documented storage policy.
